clue.text: Elderly former pupil sent back to wine-cellar

indicators.note: something sent back travels the way it came, so the phrase is read right to left

blocks.note: elderly people are aged
OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: An aged old boy of the school is packed off to a wine-cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: AGED OB, read backwards, gives BODEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, borrowed into English for a place selling or storing wine.

clue.text: A scoundrel putting on almost a quid, perhaps, in card-game

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a quid is a chew of tobacco, informally baccy
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue raises his stake by nearly a pound at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quid' looks like a pound coin; it is a chew of tobacco. BACC(Y) then A RAT, which in a down clue is put on underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game in which players bet on which hand scores closest to nine.

clue.text: Hurry up English article that's very profound

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to speed is to hurry
E is the abbreviation for English
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Hurry up with the English essay, which is very deep stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes the deepest parts of the ocean, so loosely means extremely deep.

clue.text: Reloading elaborate candlestick

indicators.note: an elaborate version is a worked-up one, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fitting fresh candles into an ornate candlestick.
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole is an ornate branched candle-holder, often with mirrors or crystal drops.

clue.text: Island where you'll find fish? Yes, heading West

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means travelling right to left, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A fishing tip: sail west for the island with fish, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGLE plus YES reversed gives ANGLESEY, an island off north-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is the large island off the north-west coast of Wales, across the Menai Strait.

clue.text: No union is in such a bad financial situation

blocks.note: no is a negative answer
Equity is the British actors' trade union

explanation.surface: Without a trade union, workers find themselves in dire money trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the name of the UK actors' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative equity is when a property is worth less than the mortgage on it, a bad financial position for the owner.

clue.text: Part of display upstairs in store

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the words that follow is taken

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Some of the exhibition is up on the top floor of a department store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a shop, but is a verb meaning put away.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay up is to put by or store, as with provisions or a boat for winter.

clue.text: Act of treachery bringing commercial success

blocks.note: first meaning: a betrayal of principles
second meaning: an event whose tickets are all bought

explanation.surface: A betrayal turns out to make someone a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is both a betrayal for gain and a show or product for which every ticket or item is bought.

clue.text: End of monarchy occurring soon in each revolutionary period

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the closing letter of the next word

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
something early happens soon

explanation.surface: The monarchy's end comes soon, in each period of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary period' sounds political; it is a year, one revolution of the Earth around the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly means once every year, and a year is the time of one orbit of the Sun.

clue.text: Location of circus business that's mainly covered by our capital

definitions.text: that's mainly covered by our capital

blocks.note: Piccadilly Circus is a famous road junction in central London
one's line is one's trade or business

explanation.surface: Where a travelling circus sets up, a business mostly covered by the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'circus' in London is a round junction, not a big top. The Piccadilly line is a London Underground route, mostly within the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piccadilly line is a London Underground route running largely under the capital, out to Heathrow.

clue.text: Moth in empty part of house

blocks.note: an empty space is clear
a wing is a section of a large house

explanation.surface: A moth is found lurking in a vacant room of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearwings are day-flying moths with largely transparent, scale-free wings, often mimicking wasps.

clue.text: Crimean War conference location

blocks.note: surface reading: where a peace conference for the Crimean War of the 1850s was held
setter's reading: a Crimean town that hosted a Second World War conference of the Allied leaders

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crimean War' reads as one phrase, the 1850s war; split it into Crimean and War conference, the 1945 meeting of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 conference of Allied leaders was held at this resort on the Crimean coast of the Black Sea.

clue.text: As it is, a dangerous substance

definitions.text: As it is, a dangerous substance

blocks.note: surface reading: a casual phrase, the way things stand

blocks.clueFragment: As it is, a dangerous substance
blocks.note: setter's reading: As is the chemical symbol of a poisonous element, so As is this substance

explanation.walkthrough: 'As it is' looks like a stock phrase, but As is the symbol for a well-known poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic, chemical symbol As, is a toxic element long notorious as a poison.

clue.text: Executes painting showing growing environment

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
an oil is a painting in oils

explanation.surface: Someone carries out a painting that depicts a garden in growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executes' looks like carries out; here it means kills, slang top.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the upper layer of earth in which plants root and grow.

clue.text: Historic Texan building in style of another state

blocks.note: à la means in the style of
MO is the abbreviation for Missouri, a US state other than Texas

explanation.surface: A historic Texas building is designed in the manner of some other state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is the old mission in San Antonio, Texas, scene of the famous 1836 siege.

clue.text: Caligula claimed he had' such a forgiving nature?

definitions.text: Caligula claimed he had' such a forgiving nature

blocks.clueFragment: Caligula claimed he had' such a forgiving nature
blocks.note: surface reading: the cruel emperor boasting of a merciful temper
setter's reading: 'to forgive, divine', so a forgiving nature is the quality of a god, which Caligula claimed to be

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'to err is human, to forgive divine' links forgiving with the quality of being a god, which Caligula claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor Caligula demanded worship as a god, claiming the status of a deity.

clue.text: He relies on daily supplies for his business

definitions.text: He relies on daily supplies for his business

blocks.clueFragment: He relies on daily supplies for his business
blocks.note: surface reading: any trader who needs fresh deliveries each day, such as a baker or greengrocer
setter's reading: dailies are daily newspapers, which this shopkeeper sells

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests fresh produce; dailies are newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a British shopkeeper selling newspapers, magazines and sweets, delivered fresh each morning.

clue.text: Cagy with omen this form of prophecy might produce

indicators.note: these letters might produce something new when made into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guarded omen could yield a kind of fortune-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Geomancy is divination by the patterns of earth, dots or lines on the ground.

clue.text: Conservative's time to lament, far from happy

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to rue is to regret or lament
feeling blue is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A Tory finds it is time to grieve, being very unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Conservative', with ''s' standing for 'is': the answer is a noun for a loyal Tory, blue being the party colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a true blue is a staunch, loyal supporter of the Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.

clue.text: South American city needs sensitivity in mob control measure

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil
tact is sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: A Brazilian city needs delicacy in how its police handle crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to order an unruly crowd to disperse.

clue.text: At which point we must admit she's objective

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the objective, or object, case of she

explanation.surface: At some point we have to concede that she has a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a goal, but it is the grammar term: the object form of she.
explanation.definitionFit: Where can mean at which place or point, as in 'the stage where we stopped'.

clue.text: Leaders of expedition may cross Islamic territory

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
cross means angry

explanation.surface: An expedition's leaders may traverse Muslim lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb of travel; it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf in the Islamic world.

clue.text: Prohibit furniture that's designed to hurt

blocks.note: to bar is to forbid
a bed is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A ban on furniture that has been made to cause injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed remark is one deliberately pointed and hurtful, like a hook with barbs.

clue.text: Exceptional case of layman somehow entering inner circle

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified route, in a new order
entering joins the jumbled letters and the circle so that one goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a circle is the shape of the letter O, here placed inside

explanation.surface: An unusual story of an outsider somehow joining the elite inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner circle' sounds like a select clique; read literally it is the round letter set inside the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something deviating from the norm, an exception to the usual rule.

clue.text: A dessert served up very cold

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the dish is read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a fool is a pudding of fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A pudding is brought to the table chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof describes a person who is distant and unfriendly, coldly detached in manner.

clue.text: Socially acceptable element?

blocks.note: surface reading: a group or person fit for polite society
setter's reading: U means upper-class, socially acceptable, and U is the symbol of a chemical element

explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like a section of society; it is a chemical element. U, the symbol, is also the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is the radioactive metallic element whose chemical symbol is U.

clue.text: Vote with the opposition party

blocks.note: first meaning, read in pieces
second meaning: a lively celebration, British slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition party' looks like one phrase; split it. The first part reads as BE A NO, joining those who vote no.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a noisy celebration or party.

clue.text: For the most part, like a wet Frankfurter?

definitions.note: a cryptic adjectival phrase for the same words

blocks.note: first meaning: generally, mostly
second meaning: a soaked resident of Frankfurt would be in the river Main, which flows through that city

explanation.walkthrough: A Frankfurter here is a person from Frankfurt, not a sausage; Frankfurt stands on the river Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on the whole or mostly, as in 'in the main, the reviews were good'.

clue.text: Having no responsibility for such cheap goods

blocks.note: first meaning, read in pieces: free of any duty
second meaning: goods sold without customs tax, as at airports

explanation.walkthrough: Duty here is both an obligation and an import tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free goods are sold without customs or excise tax, so they cost less; 'free of duty' also means unobligated.

clue.text: Tinker inserting peg of strong alloy

indicators.note: inserting means putting one thing inside another, here the second inside the first

blocks.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: A tinker hammers a peg into some tough metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a verb or a mender; here it is Shakespeare's tinker, Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means made of or resembling steel, the hard alloy of iron and carbon.
